questions.question:
ssh cka02008
A Kustomize base exists in /root/shop-kustomize/base. Create an overlay in /root/shop-kustomize/overlays/prod that:
- uses the base,
- puts all resources in namespace shop-prod,
- adds the name prefix prod-,
- sets the replicas of Deployment shop to 3.
Apply the overlay with kubectl.
questions.setup:
mkdir -p /root/shop-kustomize/base
cat <<'EOF' > /root/shop-kustomize/base/deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: shop}
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: shop}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: shop}}
    spec: {containers: [{name: shop, image: nginx:1.27-alpine}]}
EOF
cat <<'EOF' > /root/shop-kustomize/base/kustomization.yaml
resources:
- deployment.yaml
EOF
questions.meaning: Make a "prod" version of some YAML. Give it a different namespace, name prefix and replica count.
questions.words:
• base = the original YAML folder
  • overlay = a folder of changes applied on top of the base
  • kustomization.yaml = the file that lists both
  • ../../base = go up two folders, then into base

flow.h: Know what you are changing.

flow.t:
cat <<'EOF' > /root/shop-kustomize/overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml
resources:
- ../../base
namespace: shop-prod
namePrefix: prod-

questions.title: TLS ConfigMap: allow only TLSv1.3
questions.question:
ssh cka02011
Deployment nginx-static in namespace nginx-static serves HTTPS using configuration from ConfigMap nginx-config. It currently allows TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.3.
Change the configuration so that ONLY TLSv1.3 is accepted, then make the ConfigMap immutable. Make sure the running Pods use the new configuration.
keys: pods must pick up the change
questions.meaning: Edit nginx settings stored in a ConfigMap to allow only TLS 1.3. Lock the ConfigMap. Restart nginx.
questions.words:
• TLS = the encryption behind https (versions 1.2, 1.3)
  • subPath = mounts one file from a volume, updated only when the pod restarts

steps.title: Wait for nginx, then test TLS 1.2

flow.t: IP=$(k get service nginx-static -o jsonpath='{.spec.clusterIP}' -n nginx-static); echo $IP

flow.h: IP=$(...) stores the inner command's output in variable IP; -o jsonpath='{...}' prints one field. curl options: -s = quiet. -k = accept the self-signed cert. --tls-max 1.2 = offer at most TLS 1.2. Baseline: 1.2 is still accepted.
vim opens the ConfigMap. Change the line to   ssl_protocols TLSv1.3;   (keep the ;), then :wq. Change content BEFORE making it immutable.
Immutable = no more edits allowed.

flow.t: k rollout restart deployment/nginx-static -n nginx-static && k rollout status deployment/nginx-static -n nginx-static

deployment.apps/nginx-static restarted
Waiting for deployment "nginx-static" rollout to finish: 1 old replicas are pending termination...
deployment "nginx-static" successfully rolled out

flow.h: subPath files only change on pod restart.
curl -s prints nothing on failure; || echo refused prints 'refused' only when curl fails. Without --tls-max curl uses 1.3 and still gets ok. New shell? Set IP again (step 1).

questions.title: Write a NetworkPolicy: namespace AND pod selector
questions.question:
ssh cka02012
In namespace db create a NetworkPolicy named db-allow-api that allows incoming traffic to Pods labelled app=db ONLY from Pods labelled role=api in namespace api, on TCP port 80. All other incoming traffic to app=db Pods must be denied.
questions.meaning: Let only the api pods from the api namespace talk to the database. Allow port 80 only.
questions.words:
• NetworkPolicy = a firewall rule for pods
  • ingress = incoming traffic
  • namespaceSelector / podSelector = pick allowed senders by namespace label / pod label

flow.h: cat <<'EOF' > /root/np.yaml ... EOF starts a "heredoc". It writes every line up to EOF into /root/np.yaml. This is the same as pasting into vim. Same list item (no 2nd dash before podSelector) = AND. Once a policy selects app=db pods, every incoming connection it does not allow is denied.

steps.title: Check the network plugin enforces policies

flow.t:
kube-system   calico-kube-controllers-...   1/1   Running   0   ...
kube-system   canal-...                     2/2   Running   0   ...

flow.h: Only such plugins enforce NetworkPolicy (Calico may run in namespace calico-system, so -A). If none is listed, the "blocked" test will not time out. That happens even though your YAML is right. Shortened: ... marks parts of the real output left out.

flow.t: k exec api -n api -- wget -qO- -T2 db.db | head -2

flow.h: db.db = Service db in namespace db (short DNS name service.namespace). role=api in ns api passes.

flow.t: k exec web -n api -- wget -qO- -T2 db.db

wget: download timed out
command terminated with exit code 1

flow.h: role=web is denied.

questions.mug:
cat <<'EOF' > /root/np.yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: {name: db-allow-api, namespace: db}
spec:
  podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: db}}
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector: {matchLabels: {kubernetes.io/metadata.name: api}}
      podSelector: {matchLabels: {role: api}}
    ports: [{protocol: TCP, port: 80}]
EOF
k apply -f /root/np.yaml
k get pods -A | grep -E 'calico|canal|cilium'
k exec api -n api -- wget -qO- -T2 db.db | head -2
k exec web -n api -- wget -qO- -T2 db.db
k describe networkpolicy db-allow-api -n db

questions.title: Native sidecar container (restartPolicy Always)
questions.question:
ssh cka02013
Update Deployment order-app in namespace logging: add a sidecar container named log-shipper using image busybox:1.36 that runs: tail -n+1 -F /var/log/order.log
Use the native sidecar pattern (an init container with restartPolicy: Always). Share the log directory using a volume named logs mounted at /var/log in both containers. Do not change the existing container's command.
questions.setup:
kubectl create namespace logging --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: order-app, namespace: logging}
spec:
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: order-app}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: order-app}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: [sh, -c, "while true; do echo order $(date) >> /var/log/order.log; sleep 3; done"]
EOF
questions.meaning: Add a helper container that keeps reading the app log file through a shared folder. Native sidecars are stable since v1.33.
questions.words:
• init container = runs before the app starts
  • emptyDir = an empty shared folder that lives as long as the Pod

flow.t: k get deployment order-app -o yaml -n logging > /root/order-app.yaml

flow.h: Backup before big edits (restore with k replace --force -f /root/order-app.yaml).

steps.title: Add the sidecar with kubectl edit

flow.t:
spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: log-shipper

questions.title: Split node resources evenly across replicas
questions.question:
ssh cka02014
Deployment wordpress in namespace wp runs 3 replicas on node01 (it has an init container). Its Pods stay Pending.
Scale the Deployment to 0. Then give each Pod an equal share of node01's remaining CPU and memory: take node01's allocatable minus what is already requested by other Pods, keep 10% as headroom, and divide the rest by 3. Use identical requests for the init container and the main container. Scale back to 3 and ensure all Pods are Running.
questions.meaning: Share what is free on node01 fairly between 3 pods so all of them fit.
questions.words: • requests = the CPU/memory the scheduler reserves for a container

steps.title: See why the Pods are Pending

flow.t: k describe pods -l app=wordpress -n wp | grep -m1 Insufficient

NAME            READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
wordpress-...   0/1     Pending   0          1m
wordpress-...   0/1     Pending   0          1m
wordpress-...   0/1     Pending   0          1m
  Warning  FailedScheduling  ...  default-scheduler  0/2 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient cpu, 1 Insufficient memory, ...

flow.h: A Pod needs max(biggest init container, sum of main containers). The init container asks 4 CPU / 8Gi - more than node01 has. So no Pod fits, even though the main container is small. Shortened: ... marks parts of the real output left out.
Its own requests must not count while you calculate.

flow.t: k describe node node01 | grep -A7 Allocatable
k describe node node01 | grep -A6 "Allocated resources"

Allocatable:
  cpu:                1
  ephemeral-storage:  ...
  hugepages-1Gi:      0
  hugepages-2Mi:      0
  memory:             1928288Ki
  pods:               110
System Info:
Allocated resources:
  (Total limits may be over 100 percent, i.e., overcommitted.)
  Resource           Requests    Limits
  --------           --------    ------
  cpu                250m (25%)  0 (0%)
  memory             150Mi (7%)  ...
  ephemeral-storage  0 (0%)      0 (0%)

flow.h: Allocatable = what pods may use. In "Allocated resources" take the Requests column (first number), not Limits. cpu 1 = 1000m (cpu 2 = 2000m). Memory is in Ki: Ki ÷ 1024 = Mi. These are example numbers. Yours will differ - write them down.

$(( ... )) = shell integer arithmetic (it always rounds down). Put YOUR numbers in. Allocatable memory Ki ÷ 1024 = Mi. (allocatable - requested) × 90 / 100 keeps 10% headroom. Then / 3 = one Pod's share.

flow.t: k set resources deployment/wordpress -c init --requests=cpu=225m,memory=519Mi -n wp
k set resources deployment/wordpress -c wordpress --requests=cpu=225m,memory=519Mi -n wp

flow.h: -c picks the container (the init container too). Use YOUR results from the step before.

wordpress-...   1/1     Running   0          30s   ...   node01   ...

questions.title: PVC Pending: wrong StorageClass
questions.question:
ssh cka02015
PVC logs-pvc in namespace storage-fix stays Pending and Pod log-writer cannot start. Fix it so the PVC is Bound using StorageClass local-path (same name, size 200Mi, ReadWriteOnce) and the Pod is Running.
questions.setup:
kubectl get deployments -A | grep -q local-path-provisioner || kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rancher/local-path-provisioner/v0.0.30/deploy/local-path-storage.yaml
kubectl create namespace storage-fix --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: logs-pvc, namespace: storage-fix}
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: fast-ssd
  resources: {requests: {storage: 200Mi}}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: log-writer, namespace: storage-fix}
spec:
  containers:
  - {name: c, image: busybox:1.36, command: [sh, -c, "while true; do date >> /data/log; sleep 5; done"], volumeMounts: [{name: d, mountPath: /data}]}
  volumes: [{name: d, persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: logs-pvc}}]
EOF
questions.meaning: The storage request names a storage type that does not exist. Recreate it with the right type.
questions.words:
• PVC = a request for a disk
  • StorageClass = the kind of disk and who creates it (here local-path)

flow.t: k describe pvc logs-pvc -n storage-fix | tail -3

Type     Reason              Age   From                         Message
  ----     ------              ----  ----                         -------
  Warning  ProvisioningFailed  ...   persistentvolume-controller  storageclass.storage.k8s.io "fast-ssd" not found

flow.h: The class does not exist. local-path uses WaitForFirstConsumer. It creates the disk only when a Pod uses the claim. So even a correct PVC shows Pending until its Pod exists.

steps.title: Save the Pod, then delete Pod and PVC

flow.t: k get pod log-writer -o yaml -n storage-fix > /root/log-writer.yaml

flow.h: storageClassName cannot be edited on a PVC, so it must be recreated. The Pod goes first. A PVC used by a Pod is not removed. Save the Pod first so you can bring it back unchanged. A plain delete is enough for a Pending pod.

flow.t:
cat <<'EOF' > /root/logs-pvc.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: logs-pvc, namespace: storage-fix}
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: local-path
  resources: {requests: {storage: 200Mi}}
EOF

flow.h: cat <<'EOF' > /root/logs-pvc.yaml ... EOF starts a "heredoc". It writes every line up to EOF into /root/logs-pvc.yaml. This is the same as pasting into vim. Same name, size and mode; right class.

steps.title: Recreate the Pod from the saved file

flow.h: A saved object still carries resourceVersion. The API refuses to create an object that has one. The error says "resourceVersion should not be set on objects to be created". sed deletes that line (and uid). status and creationTimestamp are simply ignored.

flow.t:
NAME                             STATUS   VOLUME   CAPACITY   ACCESS MODES   STORAGECLASS   ...
persistentvolumeclaim/logs-pvc   Bound    pvc-...  200Mi      RWO            local-path     ...

NAME             READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
pod/log-writer   1/1     Running   0          40s

flow.h: local-path binds when the pod starts. This can take ~30 s. Shortened: ... marks parts of the real output left out.

questions.question:
ssh cka02016
Create a PersistentVolume app-pv: 1Gi, ReadWriteOnce, hostPath /srv/app-data, storageClassName manual.
Create a PersistentVolumeClaim app-pvc in namespace app-store requesting 500Mi from class manual.
Create a Pod app-writer (image busybox:1.36, command sleep 3600) in namespace app-store mounting the claim at /data.
questions.setup: kubectl create namespace app-store --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
questions.meaning: Make a disk, request it, and mount it into a pod.
questions.words: • hostPath = a folder on the node where the Pod runs (here usually node01)

flow.t:
cat <<'EOF' > /root/all.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata: {name: app-pv}
spec:
  capacity: {storage: 1Gi}
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: manual
  hostPath: {path: /srv/app-data}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: app-pvc, namespace: app-store}
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: manual
  resources: {requests: {storage: 500Mi}}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: app-writer, namespace: app-store}
spec:
  containers:
  - {name: c, image: busybox:1.36, command: [sleep, "3600"], volumeMounts: [{name: d, mountPath: /data}]}
  volumes: [{name: d, persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: app-pvc}}]
EOF

questions.title: NetworkPolicy blocks DNS egress
questions.question:
ssh cka03004
In namespace secure, Pod client can reach Service backend by IP but not by name. Existing NetworkPolicies must stay unchanged. Create an additional NetworkPolicy named allow-dns in namespace secure that allows all Pods in the namespace to send DNS queries (UDP and TCP 53) to the cluster DNS Pods in kube-system.
questions.meaning: A firewall rule blocks name lookups; add a rule that allows DNS only.
questions.words:
• egress = outgoing traffic
  • default-deny-egress blocks everything going out, DNS too
  • DNS = turns a name like backend into an IP (CoreDNS pods, label k8s-app=kube-dns)

flow.t: k exec client -n secure -- wget -qO- -T2 backend
k exec client -n secure -- wget -qO- -T2 $(k get pod backend -o jsonpath="{.status.podIP}" -n secure) | head -2

wget: bad address 'backend'   <-- DNS
command terminated with exit code 1
<!DOCTYPE html>               <-- IP
<html>

flow.h: The first wget takes a few seconds before "bad address". $(...) pastes the pod IP printed by the inner command (jsonpath prints one field). Classic sign: DNS (port 53) is blocked.

flow.t:
NAME          READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   LABELS
coredns-...   1/1     Running   0          ...   k8s-app=kube-dns,pod-template-hash=...
coredns-...   1/1     Running   0          ...   k8s-app=kube-dns,pod-template-hash=...

flow.h: Target for the new rule.

cat <<'EOF' > /root/dns.yaml ... EOF starts a "heredoc". It writes every line up to EOF into /root/dns.yaml. This is the same as pasting into vim. podSelector: {} = every pod in the namespace. Policies add up; this one opens only DNS.

flow.t: k exec client -n secure -- wget -qO- -T3 backend | head -2

flow.h: Name resolves and connects.

questions.mug:
k exec client -n secure -- wget -qO- -T2 backend
k exec client -n secure -- wget -qO- -T2 $(k get pod backend -o jsonpath="{.status.podIP}" -n secure) | head -2
k get pods -l k8s-app=kube-dns --show-labels -n kube-system
cat <<'EOF' > /root/dns.yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: {name: allow-dns, namespace: secure}
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: [Egress]
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector: {matchLabels: {kubernetes.io/metadata.name: kube-system}}
      podSelector: {matchLabels: {k8s-app: kube-dns}}
    ports:
    - {protocol: UDP, port: 53}
    - {protocol: TCP, port: 53}
EOF
k apply -f /root/dns.yaml
k exec client -n secure -- wget -qO- -T3 backend | head -2
k get networkpolicy -n secure
questions.docs: kubernetes.io: Network Policies (search: egress port 53)

pic.say: A firewall rule blocks name lookups; add a rule that allows DNS only. Words you need: egress = outgoing traffic; default-deny-egress blocks everything going out, DNS too; DNS = turns a name like backend into an IP (CoreDNS pods, label k8s-app=kube-dns).

story.broken: A door guard (NetworkPolicy) blocks calls to the phone book (CoreDNS) on port 53.
story.fix: Add NetworkPolicy allow-dns: egress to the kube-system DNS pods on port 53 UDP and TCP.

clues.q: can reach Service backend by IP but not by name

clues.means: Add a new policy; policies add up

clues.q: allows all Pods in the namespace
to the cluster DNS Pods in kube-system
clues.means: to: namespaceSelector kube-system AND podSelector k8s-app: kube-dns (same item), ports UDP+TCP 53

traps.dont: `- namespaceSelector` and `- podSelector` as two `to` items
traps.do: One `- namespaceSelector:` item with `podSelector: k8s-app: kube-dns` under it, because two items mean OR
List both UDP 53 and TCP 53. DNS falls back to TCP for large answers.
`policyTypes: [Egress]` only, because Ingress with no rules blocks all incoming traffic to every Pod

questions.title: CRDs: filter by group + create a custom resource
questions.question:
ssh cka03008
cert-manager CRDs are installed.
- Write the names of all CRDs belonging to API group cert-manager.io, one per line and sorted, to /root/cm-crds.txt.
- Create a ClusterIssuer named selfsigned with apiVersion cert-manager.io/v1 that uses the selfSigned issuer type.
- Save the output of kubectl explain for clusterissuer.spec.selfSigned to /root/selfsigned.txt.
questions.setup: kubectl apply -f https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/releases/download/v1.16.2/cert-manager.crds.yaml
questions.meaning: List custom types from one group, create one custom object, save its field help.
questions.words:
• CRD = adds a new object kind to Kubernetes
  • custom resource = an object of that kind (your ClusterIssuer)
  • API group = the family name of the kinds (cert-manager.io). Only the CRDs are installed (no cert-manager controller), so the issuer gets no READY status

flow.t: k get crd -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,GROUP:.spec.group --no-headers | awk '$2=="cert-manager.io"{print $1}' | sort > /root/cm-crds.txt; cat /root/cm-crds.txt

flow.h: custom-columns prints two columns, NAME and GROUP. awk '$2=="cert-manager.io"{print $1}' keeps rows whose 2nd column is exactly cert-manager.io. It prints the 1st column. sort orders them. > saves. acme.cert-manager.io items are a different group.

flow.t:
NAME                  SHORTNAMES   APIVERSION           NAMESPACED   KIND
certificaterequests   cr,crs       cert-manager.io/v1   true         CertificateRequest
certificates          cert,certs   cert-manager.io/v1   true         Certificate
clusterissuers        ciss         cert-manager.io/v1   false        ClusterIssuer   <-- cluster-wide
issuers               iss          cert-manager.io/v1   true         Issuer

flow.h: NAMESPACED false = cluster-wide.

flow.t:
cat <<'EOF' > /root/ci.yaml
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: ClusterIssuer
metadata: {name: selfsigned}
spec:
  selfSigned: {}
EOF

flow.h: cat <<'EOF' > /root/ci.yaml ... EOF starts a "heredoc". It writes every line up to EOF into /root/ci.yaml. This is the same as pasting into vim. No namespace: a ClusterIssuer is cluster-wide.
Docs come from the CRD schema.

k api-resources --api-group=cert-manager.io
cat <<'EOF' > /root/ci.yaml

kind: ClusterIssuer

  selfSigned: {}
EOF
k apply -f /root/ci.yaml

cat /root/cm-crds.txt

questions.title: Gateway API: header match + weighted split
questions.question:
ssh cka03010
In namespace shop-gw a Gateway shop-gw (HTTP, port 80) and Services shop-v1 and shop-v2 exist.
Create an HTTPRoute named shop-route attached to shop-gw for hostname shop.example.com:
- Requests with header x-version: v2 go 100% to shop-v2.
- All other requests are split 80% shop-v1 and 20% shop-v2.
Both Services listen on port 80.
questions.setup:
kubectl get crd gateways.gateway.networking.k8s.io >/dev/null 2>&1 || kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/download/v1.2.1/standard-install.yaml
kubectl create namespace shop-gw --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: GatewayClass
metadata: {name: cka-demo}
spec: {controllerName: example.net/gateway-controller}
---
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata: {name: shop-gw, namespace: shop-gw}
spec:
  gatewayClassName: cka-demo
  listeners: [{name: http, protocol: HTTP, port: 80}]
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: shop-v1, namespace: shop-gw}
spec: {selector: {app: shop, v: "1"}, ports: [{port: 80}]}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: shop-v2, namespace: shop-gw}
spec: {selector: {app: shop, v: "2"}, ports: [{port: 80}]}
EOF
questions.meaning: Send testers (header v2) to version 2 and split everyone else 80/20.
questions.words:
• Gateway = the entry point that listens (HTTP port 80)
  • GatewayClass = which controller runs it
  • HTTPRoute = routing rules attached to a Gateway
  • parentRefs = which Gateway
  • backendRefs = which Services get the traffic

flow.t: k get gateway shop-gw -o yaml -n shop-gw | grep -A6 listeners

listeners:
  - allowedRoutes:
      namespaces:
        from: Same
    name: http
    port: 80
    protocol: HTTP

flow.h: Route will attach to this listener (allowedRoutes Same = routes from this namespace).

flow.t:
cat <<'EOF' > /root/route.yaml
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata: {name: shop-route, namespace: shop-gw}
spec:
  parentRefs: [{name: shop-gw}]
  hostnames: [shop.example.com]
  rules:
  - matches:
    - headers: [{name: x-version, value: v2}]
    backendRefs: [{name: shop-v2, port: 80}]
  - matches:
    - path: {type: PathPrefix, value: /}
    backendRefs:
    - {name: shop-v1, port: 80, weight: 80}
    - {name: shop-v2, port: 80, weight: 20}
EOF

flow.h: cat <<'EOF' > /root/route.yaml ... EOF starts a "heredoc". It writes every line up to EOF into /root/route.yaml. This is the same as pasting into vim. Rule 1 has no path, so it also matches path /. With equal paths, Gateway API picks the rule with more header matches. So x-version: v2 requests go 100% to shop-v2.

flow.t: k describe httproute shop-route -n shop-gw | grep -A30 Rules

Rules:
    Backend Refs:
...
      Name:    shop-v2
      Port:    80
      Weight:  1
    Matches:
      Headers:
        Name:   x-version   <-- rule 1
        Type:   Exact
        Value:  v2
...
      Name:    shop-v1
      Port:    80
      Weight:  80          <-- rule 2
...
      Name:    shop-v2
      Port:    80
      Weight:  20
...

questions.title: NetworkPolicy pick: AND vs OR trap
questions.question:
ssh cka03011
Pods labelled app=api in namespace payments must accept traffic ONLY from Pods labelled app=gateway in namespace edge, on TCP port 80. A default deny-ingress policy exists in payments.
Several candidate policies are in /root/netpols-ex/. Apply the single file that meets the requirement with the least privilege. Do not modify any file or existing policy.
questions.meaning: Pick the rule where namespace AND pod label must both match, on port 80 only.
questions.words: • least privilege = allow only what is needed, nothing more

flow.t: for f in /root/netpols-ex/*.yaml; do echo "== $f"; cat $f; done

flow.h: for f in ...; do ...; done repeats cat for every file. Each "-" under from: starts a separate OR item. a = OR: every pod in edge, OR app=gateway pods in payments. Alone, podSelector means the policy's own namespace. b = AND + TCP 80. c = right senders but EVERY port. d = all edge pods to all payments pods. b is the only least-privilege match.
One file, no edits.

flow.t: k exec gateway -n edge -- wget -qO- -T2 api.payments | head -2
k exec intruder -n edge -- wget -qO- -T2 api.payments

<!DOCTYPE html>                       <-- gateway
<html>
wget: download timed out              <-- intruder
command terminated with exit code 1

flow.h: Only the gateway pod gets in. If the intruder is NOT blocked, check the network plugin enforces policies. Run k get pods -A | grep -E 'calico|canal|cilium'.

questions.title: HPA: CPU + memory, scaleUp and scaleDown behavior
questions.question:
ssh cka03013
Create a HorizontalPodAutoscaler named worker-hpa in namespace metrics-app for Deployment worker:
- min 2, max 6 replicas,
- target 60% average CPU utilisation AND 70% average memory utilisation,
- scale up by at most 2 Pods per 60 seconds,
- scale-down stabilization window of 120 seconds.
questions.meaning: Autoscale on CPU and memory. Add at most 2 pods a minute. Remove pods only after 2 calm minutes.
questions.words:
• HPA = HorizontalPodAutoscaler, adds/removes pods automatically
  • utilisation = usage ÷ request, in %

flow.t:
cat <<'EOF' > /root/hpa.yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata: {name: worker-hpa, namespace: metrics-app}
spec:
  scaleTargetRef: {apiVersion: apps/v1, kind: Deployment, name: worker}
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 6
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource: {name: cpu, target: {type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 60}}
  - type: Resource
    resource: {name: memory, target: {type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 70}}
  behavior:
    scaleUp:
      policies:
      - {type: Pods, value: 2, periodSeconds: 60}
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 120
EOF

flow.h: cat <<'EOF' > /root/hpa.yaml ... EOF starts a "heredoc". It writes every line up to EOF into /root/hpa.yaml. This is the same as pasting into vim. Two metrics: HPA computes replicas for each and uses the higher. scaleUp policy Pods 2 / 60 s = add at most 2 pods per minute. scaleDown stabilizationWindowSeconds 120 = look back 2 min before removing pods. It acts on the highest recommendation of the last 2 min.

flow.t:

flow.h: Real % instead of <unknown> if metrics-server runs. <unknown> = no metrics (yet); the config is still right.

flow.t:

worker   2/2     2            2           2m

questions.meaning: Create a priority just under the top one. Allow it to push others out. Give it to a deployment.
questions.words:
• PriorityClass = a named number, higher = scheduled first
  • globalDefault = the class used by pods that name none

flow.t:
NAME        VALUE
batch-low   100
team-a      3000
team-b      7000  <-- highest

flow.h: Lowest to highest; the last line is the highest. --sort-by sorts ascending. custom-columns prints only name and value. grep -v system- hides the system-* classes.

flow.t:
cat <<'EOF' > /root/pc.yaml
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata: {name: critical-jobs}
value: 6999
globalDefault: false
preemptionPolicy: PreemptLowerPriority
description: "critical batch"
EOF

flow.h: cat <<'EOF' > /root/pc.yaml ... EOF starts a "heredoc". It writes every line up to EOF into /root/pc.yaml. This is the same as pasting into vim. PreemptLowerPriority (the default) = may evict lower-priority pods to make room. Do NOT copy Never from team-b.
Replaces batch-low; changing the pod template starts a rollout.

flow.t:
deployment "payments-api" successfully rolled out
NAME              PRIO   CLASS
payments-api-...  6999   critical-jobs
payments-api-...  6999   critical-jobs

flow.h: Priority is copied into each new pod.

questions.title: StorageClass (Retain, expandable) + StatefulSet claims
questions.question:
ssh cka03015
Create a StorageClass named retain-local: provisioner rancher.io/local-path, reclaimPolicy Retain, volumeBindingMode WaitForFirstConsumer, allowVolumeExpansion true. It must NOT be the default.
In namespace cache create a StatefulSet cache (2 replicas, image redis:7-alpine, headless Service cache) with a volumeClaimTemplate named data requesting 100Mi from retain-local, mounted at /data.
keys: sc = retain-local (Retain, WFFC, expandable, not default)
questions.setup:
kubectl get deployments -A | grep -q local-path-provisioner || kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rancher/local-path-provisioner/v0.0.30/deploy/local-path-storage.yaml
kubectl create namespace cache --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
questions.meaning: Make a storage type that keeps disks after delete. Make a 2-pod database that gets one disk each.
questions.words:
• StatefulSet = pods with stable names (cache-0, cache-1) and one disk each
  • headless Service = gives those pods DNS names
  • reclaimPolicy Retain = keep the disk after its claim is deleted

flow.t:
cat <<'EOF' > /root/sc.yaml
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata: {name: retain-local}
provisioner: rancher.io/local-path
reclaimPolicy: Retain
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
allowVolumeExpansion: true
EOF

flow.h: cat <<'EOF' > /root/sc.yaml ... EOF starts a "heredoc". It writes every line up to EOF into /root/sc.yaml. This is the same as pasting into vim. No default annotation = not default.
Each replica gets its own PVC, named <template>-<statefulset>-<number> = data-cache-0, data-cache-1.

flow.t:
NAME          READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
pod/cache-0   1/1     Running   0          60s
pod/cache-1   1/1     Running   0          40s

NAME                                 STATUS   VOLUME   CAPACITY   ACCESS MODES   STORAGECLASS   ...
persistentvolumeclaim/data-cache-0   Bound    pvc-...  100Mi      RWO            retain-local   ...
persistentvolumeclaim/data-cache-1   Bound    pvc-...  100Mi      RWO            retain-local   ...
pvc-...   100Mi   RWO   Retain   Bound   cache/data-cache-0   retain-local   ...   <-- pv
pvc-...   100Mi   RWO   Retain   Bound   cache/data-cache-1   retain-local   ...

flow.h: cache-0 starts first, then cache-1 (wait for the redis pull). PVs keep the Retain policy. Shortened: ... marks parts of the real output left out.

questions.mug:
cat <<'EOF' > /root/sc.yaml
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata: {name: retain-local}
provisioner: rancher.io/local-path
reclaimPolicy: Retain
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
allowVolumeExpansion: true
EOF
k apply -f /root/sc.yaml
cat <<'EOF' > /root/sts.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: cache, namespace: cache}
spec: {clusterIP: None, selector: {app: cache}, ports: [{port: 6379}]}
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata: {name: cache, namespace: cache}
spec:
  serviceName: cache
  replicas: 2
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: cache}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: cache}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - {name: redis, image: redis:7-alpine, volumeMounts: [{name: data, mountPath: /data}]}
  volumeClaimTemplates:
  - metadata: {name: data}
    spec:
      accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
      storageClassName: retain-local
      resources: {requests: {storage: 100Mi}}
EOF
k apply -f /root/sts.yaml
k get pods,pvc -n cache
k get pv | grep retain-local
k get storageclass retain-local
k get pvc -n cache

pic.say: Make a storage type that keeps disks after delete. Make a 2-pod database that gets one disk each. Words you need: StatefulSet = pods with stable names (cache-0, cache-1) and one disk each; headless Service = gives those pods DNS names; reclaimPolicy Retain = keep the disk after its claim is deleted.

story.broken: No room type retain-local exists, and the cache dishes have no store rooms.
story.fix: Create StorageClass retain-local (Retain, expandable), then StatefulSet cache with volumeClaimTemplates.

coach.pattern: StorageClass fields + StatefulSet with volumeClaimTemplates

clues.q: reclaimPolicy Retain, volumeBindingMode WaitForFirstConsumer, allowVolumeExpansion true
clues.means: Three top-level SC fields (not under spec)

clues.q: It must NOT be the default
with a volumeClaimTemplate named data requesting 100Mi from retain-local

traps.do: Put provisioner, reclaimPolicy, volumeBindingMode, allowVolumeExpansion at the top level, because StorageClass has no spec
`serviceName: cache`, matching the headless Service cache, so Pods get stable DNS names
`volumeMounts: - name: data, mountPath: /data`, because it must match the volumeClaimTemplate name data

questions.title: Re-bind a Released PV (clear claimRef)
questions.question:
ssh cka03016
The PostgreSQL data PersistentVolume pg-data-pv still holds data, but it is in Released state after its old claim was deleted.
- Make the PV available again WITHOUT deleting it or its data.
- Create PVC pg-data in namespace postgres (1Gi, ReadWriteOnce, storageClassName manual) that binds to it.
- Deploy /root/pg-deploy.yaml (already uses claim pg-data) and make sure the Pod is Running.
questions.meaning: An old disk is "locked" to a deleted claim. Unlock it, claim it again, and start the database.
questions.words:
• Released = old claim gone, but the PV is still reserved for it
  • claimRef = that reservation inside the PV
  • reclaimPolicy Retain = the disk and data are kept when the claim is deleted

flow.t:
NAME         CAPACITY   ACCESS MODES   RECLAIM POLICY   STATUS     CLAIM                   STORAGECLASS   ...
pg-data-pv   1Gi        RWO            Retain           Released   postgres/old-pg-claim   manual         ...

flow.h: Released PVs never bind again by themselves. Shortened: ... marks parts of the real output left out.
The --type=json patch {"op":"remove","path":"/spec/claimRef"} deletes the claimRef field. Or run k edit pv/pg-data-pv and delete the claimRef block. Frees the PV; data stays on disk.

flow.t:
NAME         CAPACITY   ACCESS MODES   RECLAIM POLICY   STATUS      CLAIM   STORAGECLASS   ...
pg-data-pv   1Gi        RWO            Retain           Available           manual         ...

flow.h: Ready for a new claim. Check this first, so you know the patch worked. Shortened: ... marks parts of the real output left out.

flow.t:
cat <<'EOF' > /root/pvc.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: pg-data, namespace: postgres}
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: manual
  resources: {requests: {storage: 1Gi}}
EOF

flow.h: cat <<'EOF' > /root/pvc.yaml ... EOF starts a "heredoc". It writes every line up to EOF into /root/pvc.yaml. This is the same as pasting into vim. Class + size + mode match the PV.

flow.t:
deployment.apps/postgres created
NAME                            STATUS   VOLUME       CAPACITY   ACCESS MODES   STORAGECLASS   ...
persistentvolumeclaim/pg-data   Bound    pg-data-pv   1Gi        RWO            manual         ...

NAME               READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
pod/postgres-...   1/1     Running   0          70s

pic.say: An old disk is "locked" to a deleted claim. Unlock it, claim it again, and start the database. Words you need: Released = old claim gone, but the PV is still reserved for it; claimRef = that reservation inside the PV; reclaimPolicy Retain = the disk and data are kept when the claim is deleted.

story.broken: Store room pg-data-pv still holds data but is Released: still tied to an old slip.
story.fix: Remove spec.claimRef from the PV, then create PVC pg-data to bind it.

coach.pattern: Released PV → remove claimRef → new PVC binds

clues.means: spec.claimRef still points to the old PVC → remove it

clues.q: WITHOUT deleting it or its data
clues.means: k patch pv to remove claimRef (no delete)

clues.q: (1Gi, ReadWriteOnce, storageClassName manual) that binds to it
clues.means: PVC must match the PV's size, mode and class

traps.dont: `k delete pv pg-data-pv` and recreate it
traps.do: Remove only the claimRef: `k patch pv pg-data-pv --type=json` with op remove, path /spec/claimRef. It frees the PV and keeps the data

traps.dont: Create the PVC without checking the patch worked
traps.do: `k get pv pg-data-pv` must show Available first, so you know the patch worked

traps.dont: Create PVC pg-data in namespace default
traps.do: Set `namespace: postgres` on PVC pg-data. A Pod can only use claims in its own namespace.

k apply -f /root/pg-deploy.yaml; k get pvc,pods -n postgres
coach.plan: PV Released (old claimRef) → patch: remove /spec/claimRef → Available → PVC pg-data (manual, 1Gi, RWO) → apply pg-deploy.yaml → Bound + Running
